chunks: From him, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
'To satiate a man from my brethren is more beloved to me than if I were to enter this market of yours, buy a head from it, and free him.'

key_terms.أُشْبِعَ: to satiate or fill with food
key_terms.رَأْساً: a head (referring to a slave's head/freedom)

ai.seo_question: What is the virtue of feeding a fellow believer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the simple act of feeding a brother above the significant spiritual milestone of manumitting a slave, emphasizing the immediacy and accessibility of sustaining the believer's physical needs. This comparison underscores the profound social bond of *ikhwa* (brotherhood) in Shia tradition, where satisfying hunger is viewed as a direct manifestation of divine mercy and communal solidarity.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ismail Bin Mihran, from Safwan Al Jammal, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘If I were to satiate a man from my brethren, it would be more beloved to me than if I<sup>asws</sup> were to enter this market of theirs, and buy a head from him, so I<sup>asws</sup> free him’.
en.sarwar: 14. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Isma’il ibn Mehran from Safwan al-Jammal from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Feeding one of my brothers (in belief) to his satisfaction is more beloved to me than entering your market to buy a slave and set him free.”
